title: Sky-pooler cutover leaves index-4 unmintable: newPooler._minter never set to NFTMinterV2, mint(4) reverts
variantNote: Affects both run variants. :dry (preview/dry-mode) produces a FALSE GREEN — _step16_postStateLog asserts configs(4)==newPooler, hook rotation, BPT migration, sUSDS drain, but never asserts mint(4)/_minter, so it reports 'All post-state invariants hold'. :broadcast then ACTUALLY breaks — steps 3-14 re-point the dispatcher and sweep funds but newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) is never called, leaving ATokenDispatcher._minter == address(0) and mint(4) reverting for all users.
description: The Story-056 Sky-pooler cutover script (DispatcherReplaceSkyPoolerAtIndex4.s.sol) deploys a fresh BalancerPoolerV2 (the new index-4 pooler / ATokenDispatcher), re-points configs(4).dispatcher to it via replaceDispatcher(4, newPooler) (confirmed at script line 523), rotates the phUSD mint hook (setMinter at 333/534), migrates the BPT, and drains sUSDS. However, it never calls newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2). The freshly deployed ATokenDispatcher's internal _minter therefore stays at its default address(0) (ATokenDispatcher.sol:14). NFTMinterV2.mint(4) routes through dispatcher.dispatch(), which is gated by the onlyMinter modifier require(msg.sender == _minter, 'ATokenDispatcher: caller is not minter') (ATokenDispatcher.sol:25-26, 82). With _minter == address(0), that require can never pass, so mint(4) reverts for every caller from the moment the cutover broadcasts. The script's dry-mode post-condition epilogue _step16_postStateLog (lines 603-657) verifies the dispatcher pointer, hook rotation, BPT migration and sUSDS drain but contains NO mint(4) or _minter invariant, so a preview run reports all invariants holding (false green) while the broadcast path ships the break to production.
impact: Complete availability break of the core, user-facing protocol function the cutover exists to preserve: index-4 NFT minting. From the instant the cutover broadcasts until a privileged owner follow-up transaction is sent, every NFTMinterV2.mint(4) call reverts 'ATokenDispatcher: caller is not minter'. No assets are stolen, lost, or compromised — user funds, BPT, and the migrated sUSDS/Sky-route positions remain safe and fully recoverable — but the primary product function for index 4 is fully bricked. Because the script's own dry-mode self-check passes green (no mint(4)/_minter assertion), the defect is likely to reach production undetected and is only discovered when the first user mint(4) reverts.
attackPath: 1. Operator runs the cutover in PREVIEW/dry mode; _step16_postStateLog asserts configs(4)==newPooler, hook rotation, BPT migration, sUSDS drain, but never asserts mint(4)/_minter, so it reports 'All post-state invariants hold' (false green).

2. Trusting the green dry run, the operator broadcasts; steps 3-14 apply (dispatcher re-pointed to newPooler, funds swept) but newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) is never called, leaving ATokenDispatcher._minter == address(0).
3. Any user calls NFTMinterV2.mint(4); mint() invokes dispatcher.dispatch(), whose onlyMinter modifier requires msg.sender == _minter; with _minter == 0 the require always fails.

4. Index-4 minting is denied for all users until the owner sends a corrective newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) transaction (the predecessor cutover's documented pattern, SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler.s.sol).

evidence.scriptMissingCall: DispatcherReplaceSkyPoolerAtIndex4.s.sol contains setMinter only as phUSD.setMinter(newHook/oldHook) (lines 333, 534) and an interface declaration (656); there is no newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) anywhere in the cutover sequence (steps 3-15).
evidence.dispatcherGate: lib/yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/ATokenDispatcher.sol:14 declares 'address internal _minter' (defaults to 0); lines 25-26 'modifier onlyMinter { require(msg.sender == _minter, "ATokenDispatcher: caller is not minter"); }'; setMinter is owner-only (lines 61-62).
evidence.falseGreenPostCondition: _step16_postStateLog (lines 603-657) asserts the dispatcher pointer (configs(4)==newPooler, line 523), hook rotation, BPT migration and sUSDS drain, but encodes no mint(4)/_minter invariant.
evidence.forkProof: Verified on mainnet fork (block 25241930): cutover-then-mint(4) reverts with the exact error 'ATokenDispatcher: caller is not minter'; mint(4) succeeds only after newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) is applied. PoC: workspace/phoenix-phase-2-staging/test/AuditSkyPoolerMintIndex4.t.sol.

recommendation: Add newPooler.setMinter(NFT_MINTER_V2) to the cutover sequence (mirroring SetMinterOnIndex4Pooler.s.sol) so the fresh dispatcher's _minter is authorized atomically as part of the broadcast, AND add a post-condition to _step16_postStateLog that asserts the index-4 mint path actually works (e.g. assert newPooler.minter()==NFT_MINTER_V2, or a static-call mint(4) probe) so the dry run can no longer report a false green over a bricked mint path.
relatedNote: Same root-cause class as the ledger's open RestoreMintAtIndex4 finding (skipped setMinter on a fresh index-4 pooler), different contract/script and different entryPoint. Not a regression: distinct per-entryPoint fingerprint, not previously marked fixed.

classification.flagReason: Borderline High/Medium. Deliberate downgrade from proposed High: total availability break of a core function but zero asset risk and single-tx privileged recovery. Reasoning recorded in classification report (CLASS-001).
classification.reasoning: C4 High requires assets stolen/lost/compromised; here no assets are at risk (funds safe and fully recoverable) and the only outcome is a core-function availability break — C4 Medium. Not lowered to QA because the availability break is concrete, fork-verified, total for the affected function, and ships to production behind a false-green self-check.
